newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Stadium Australia says float shortfall A$214.3 mln.
newsitem.headline: Stadium Australia says float shortfall A$214.3 mln.

text.p: The underwriters to the A$364.4 million Stadium Australia float said on Friday there had been a A$214.3 million shortfall for the float and that they had fully subscribed to this shortfall.
The underwriters were ANZ Securities, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Macquarie Bank Ltd and ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.

"The underwriters of the Stadium Australia Offers today confirmed that the Gold Package Offer which closed on March 27 was under-subscribed and have announced that planning will commence immediately for the next marketing phase," Stadium Australia said.
Stadium Australia offered 35,000 passes which included packages of main stadium tickets to the Sydney 2000 Olympics, a 30-year stadium membership and an equity stake in the stadium itself.
The Stadium Australia float, which closed last Thursday, had been open for almost six months, more than twice as long as most share offers.
Its offer of 34,400 gold packages at A$10,000 each and 600 platinum passes at A$33,000 each opened on October 7 and its closing date has been extended twice due to lack of demand.
Stadium Australia said the platinum packages were over-subscribed.

Stadium Australia Management chief executive Chris Chapman said the under-subscription of the float had no bearing on the construction of the Stadium or its future progress as the stadium was fully underwritten and payment had been received in full.@
"Time is on our side. There is no question that the gold packages will in fact appreciate in value as we get closer to the Sydney 2000 Olympic Games."
The packages, minus the Olympic tickets which detach from the membership and equity components, are expected to list on the stock exchange around April 11.
